headline: A Philadelphia coding programme is rebuilding its courses around AI skills because entry-level tech jobs have dried up, Chalkbeat reports.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a clear local example of AI hitting entry-level tech work, but it covers one programme and 12 graduates.
importance_line: Young people without college degrees who trained to code are the ones affected, but this is one programme's experience, not national data.
summary: Chalkbeat Philadelphia reports that Launchpad Philly, a nonprofit that trains high school students and recent graduates to code, is reworking its curriculum around AI skills because entry-level tech jobs have dried up as companies cut jobs and lean on AI for basic tasks. Of its first intensive cohort of 12 graduates, three now work full time and two are in college, and trainee Daniel Johnson, 20, says he has not had a single reply to his job applications.
notes: Pool item was the 9 Oct newsletter version; the full 8 Oct article was read and linked. Published 8 Oct, within the scan window; treated as NEW.
